A.explanation: With $x = 907\text{ m}$ the water layer is too thick, so $\rho_{oil}gx + \rho_{water}g(2000 - x)$ is about $18.1\text{ MPa}$, greater than $17.5\text{ MPa}$.

B.explanation: With $x = 1000\text{ m}$ the two layers are equal, giving about $18.0\text{ MPa}$, still greater than the measured $17.5\text{ MPa}$.

C.explanation: With $x = 1090\text{ m}$ the oil layer is still too thin, giving about $17.8\text{ MPa}$, greater than $17.5\text{ MPa}$.

D.explanation: With $x$ about $1270\text{ m}$ the sum of the oil pressure and water pressure equals $17.5\text{ MPa}$, matching the given bottom pressure.

hints: Notice the 2000 m borehole is split into oil of depth $x$ on top and water of depth $2000 - x$ below it.
Connect this to hydrostatic pressure: total pressure is $p = \rho_{oil}gx + \rho_{water}g(2000 - x)$ with densities $830\text{ kg m}^{-3}$ and $1000\text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
Set that sum equal to $17.5\text{ MPa}$ and solve the linear equation for $x$, remembering $1\text{ MPa} = 10^6\text{ Pa}$.
walkthrough: Identify the layers from the diagram: oil depth $= x$ and water depth $= 2000 - x$, both in $\text{m}$, with total liquid pressure $17.5 \times 10^6\text{ Pa}$ at the bottom.
State the rule: pressure due to a liquid column is $p = \rho g h$, so the bottom pressure is the sum $p = \rho_{oil}gx + \rho_{water}g(2000 - x)$.
Divide by $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to simplify: $830x + 1000(2000 - x) = 17.5 \times 10^6 / 9.81 \approx 1783900\text{ kg m}^{-2}$.
A larger $x$ means more low-density oil, which lowers the total pressure below the all-water value, as required. This is option D.
